Thin a visit schedule with missed visits and dropout (C1)

Source: R/interval_censoring.R
thin_visits.Rd

Layers schedule-only randomness on top of a fixed visit schedule – no simulated outcome is read, so this is the "safe", always- non-informative member of the visit-process generators (contrast with visit_schedule_informative, which reads the simulated outcome by design). Each non-baseline visit is independently missed with probability p_miss; independently of that, each subject may also start dropping out: with probability p_dropout, one of their non-baseline visits is chosen uniformly at random as the dropout onset, and it and every later visit is dropped. The baseline visit (time = 0) is never dropped by either mechanism.

Usage

thin_visits(visits, p_miss = 0, p_dropout = 0, ids = NULL, seed = NULL)

Arguments

visits

A per-subject schedule (a data frame with ID/ time columns, e.g. from visit_schedule), or a common numeric vector – in which case ids is required, and the vector is expanded to one copy per ID first (via the same internal validation add_interval_censoring itself uses).

p_miss, p_dropout

Numeric scalars in [0, 1], default 0 (no thinning; visits is returned as given). The dropout-onset visit is drawn from the subject's original non-baseline visits, independently of any p_miss draws for that subject.

ids

Required only when visits is a numeric vector; the subject IDs to expand it across (e.g. events$ID).

seed

Optional integer. If supplied, set.seed(seed) is called before any draw. Leave NULL inside a larger already-seeded workflow.

Value

A data frame with ID/time columns – a (possibly shorter, per subject) schedule directly usable as add_interval_censoring's visits argument. Must be applied before add_interval_censoring, and composes with add_censoring in either relative order (they touch disjoint objects: this function only ever reads/writes a visit schedule, never events).

See also

visit_schedule, which builds the schedule to thin; visit_schedule_informative, the outcome-reactive counterpart; add_interval_censoring, which takes the thinned schedule as visits.

Examples

sched <- visit_schedule(n = 20, every = 4, end = 24, seed = 1)
thinned <- thin_visits(sched, p_miss = 0.1, p_dropout = 0.05, seed = 2)
nrow(thinned) <= nrow(sched)
#> [1] TRUE
